trail.text: Investigating the spike — mapping deviating services to find the root.
Auth service shows major resource pressure while others show only tail latency — checking if it's source or victim.
Auth backend looks healthy, pointing to auth itself — checking event timing to confirm the cascade order.
Timing suggests host disk activity preceded auth slowdown — verifying the sequence before ranking.
Early signals are clustering — pulling detailed series to confirm the origin.
Auth memory tripled right after the flag — ruling out other hosts before finalizing.

causes.reasoning: Auth shows massive internal pressure (memory failures 0.8->90970, working-set 162M->422M, cpu-system 0.27->13.27) with median latency 0.18->0.80 while its mongo backend is flat, indicating origin not victim.
Single host shows 40x disk write spike (1.9->75.7) and read spike with memory-active 69M->380M while other hosts flat, consistent with co-located auth pressure spilling to host IO.
Tail latency 0.024->0.197 with flat container CPU/memory indicates victim waiting on slow downstream, exceeding later at 43s after auth degraded.
p99 latency 0.048->0.337 with p50/p90 and resources flat indicates tail victim of upstream slowdown, not internal exhaustion.
Frontend latency 0.23->1.09 with flat CPU/memory reflects aggregation of downstream auth-related delays, typical caller-victim pattern.
